docs.disclosure.a11y.actions: The actions are outside the heading and the button, so they are not part of the name and never toggle the region. Give each one its own accessible name.
docs.disclosure.a11y.focus: The focus stays on the button when it opens and when it closes. When the region closes with the focus inside it, for example from a button in the region, the focus goes to the button of the disclosure and not to the page.
docs.disclosure.a11y.heading: With headingLevel the button is inside a heading of that level, so a screen reader lists the section. Choose the level that fits the outline of your page. Without it there is no heading, which is right for something that is not one, such as a folder in a tree.
docs.disclosure.a11y.hidden: A closed region has the hidden attribute: it is out of the tab order and away from screen readers, and its content stays mounted. Do not set display on the region itself, which would win over hidden.
docs.disclosure.a11y.keyboard: Enter and Space open and close it, as on any button, and Tab reaches it in the order of the page. Nothing inside the region can be reached while it is closed.
docs.disclosure.a11y.motion: The chevron turns over 120 ms. With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce it turns at once, without an animation.
docs.disclosure.a11y.name: The summary is the name of the button and it does not change when the region opens: aria-expanded says it. The chevron is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Describe the button with aria-describedby in buttonProps.
docs.disclosure.a11y.pattern: It follows the ARIA disclosure pattern: a native button with aria-expanded and an aria-controls that points at the region.
docs.disclosure.a11y.strings: Disclosure has no text of its own: the summary and the region are yours, in your language.
docs.disclosure.api.actions: Only for section. Controls at the end of the header, outside the button, such as the trigger of a Menu. Pressing one never opens or closes the region.
docs.disclosure.api.buttonProps: Attributes of the button that the disclosure does not set: aria-describedby, aria-label, className, id, disabled… The disclosure keeps type, aria-expanded, aria-controls, onClick and ref.
docs.disclosure.api.children: The region: what the button shows and hides. It sits right under the button or the header.
docs.disclosure.api.className: A class for the element around the button and the region, to lay it out where it goes. For the button, use buttonProps.
docs.disclosure.api.defaultOpen: Whether the region starts open, when open is not passed.
docs.disclosure.api.headingLevel: Only for section. Puts the button inside a heading of that level, so the section is in the outline of the page. Leave it out where the summary is not a heading, such as a folder in a tree.
docs.disclosure.api.onOpenChange: Called with the next state when the button is pressed, controlled or not.
docs.disclosure.api.open: Whether the region is open. Passing it makes the disclosure controlled: it shows what you pass, and without onOpenChange it never opens.
docs.disclosure.api.summary: The visible content of the button: text, or a row of nodes such as an icon and a name. It is inside a button, so it must not hold a link.
docs.disclosure.api.variant: inline is a block for a line or a row of content, not for the inside of a paragraph (use DisclosureButton for a button in a sentence), and section is for the heading of a part of the page.
docs.disclosure.button.chevron: Which side of the summary the chevron goes: end for a line of content, start for the heading of a section.
docs.disclosure.group.parts.description: When the row around the button holds a link, the button cannot hold the row. Build it from DisclosureRoot, DisclosureButton and DisclosureRegion, and put the region where it belongs.
docs.disclosure.group.parts.title: Parts
docs.disclosure.group.states.description: Uncontrolled, it keeps its own state. Controlled, the application holds it with open and onOpenChange. A disabled button cannot open it.
docs.disclosure.group.variants.descripti: inline is a block: a button with its chevron after the text, and the region under it. It draws a div, so it cannot go inside a paragraph. section is the heading of a part of the page: the chevron comes first and the actions sit beside the button.
docs.disclosure.group.variants.title: Variants
docs.disclosure.hint.controlled: The application keeps open. Press Done: the region closes and the focus goes to the button, not to the page.
docs.disclosure.hint.defaultOpen: It starts open, and the button still closes it. Without open the disclosure keeps its own state.
docs.disclosure.hint.disabled: A disabled button leaves the tab order and cannot be pressed. Its summary still says what is there.
docs.disclosure.hint.inline: Open it with Enter or Space. The focus stays on the button.
docs.disclosure.hint.parts: The sentence has a link, so the button is only a part of the row and the sentence describes it. The list goes under the whole row.
docs.disclosure.hint.section: The button is inside a level 3 heading. The menu beside it is outside the button: pressing it does not open or close the folder.
docs.disclosure.limit.button: There is no ref on the button and no onClick: onOpenChange reports every change.
docs.disclosure.limit.direction: The chevron is drawn for left-to-right text: it points right while the region is closed. It is not mirrored for right-to-left languages yet.
docs.disclosure.limit.group: A group of disclosures where opening one closes the others is not part of it. Control each one with open and keep which one is open yourself.
docs.disclosure.limit.mounted: The region stays mounted while it is closed, so its content keeps its state and is rendered even if nobody opens it. To render it only when it is open, control the disclosure and write the content as '{open && …}', where open is the state you pass to it.
docs.disclosure.limit.parts: A link or another control cannot go in the summary, because it would be inside a button. When it has to sit in the same row, use DisclosureRoot, DisclosureButton and DisclosureRegion: the button is a part of the row and the region goes where you place it.
docs.disclosure.limit.touch: Below 768 px the button is 44 px tall, a touch target, so an inline one makes its line taller there. A link in the same sentence as an inline button is outside it and keeps its own size.
docs.disclosure.root.children: A DisclosureButton and a DisclosureRegion, wherever you place them.
docs.disclosure.summary: A button that shows and hides a region, as a line of content or as the heading of a section.
docs.disclosure.usage.description: Import Disclosure, give it a summary and write the region as its children. The button carries aria-expanded and aria-controls, and the region is hidden while it is closed.
